cultural.vision_reason: This is a hand drum with drumstick, painted with a Namgis (Kwakwaka'wakw) sun face design by named artist William Wasden Jr., a well-known Kwakwaka'wakw carver/painter — a clear match for the claimed people and category.

physical.title: drum; drum-stick
physical.summary: Drum (with drum-stick); made of skin; a) frame of drum made of small rectangles of carved wood glued together side by side to form circle; skin stretched over circular frame, tied across back with sinew; leather wrapped around centre of sinew to make handle; front painted with image of face with rays around it in red with green and black facial features and red mouth on green background; "William Wasden Jr Hilamas 2005 Namgis Sun" written in pencil on back of skin; b) drum-stick carved of piece of wood, one end wrapped with leather and stuffed for drum-stick head; strip of leather tied to opposite end of handle for carrying strap.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a carved wooden bird-form (Thunderbird) rattle with black-and-red formline painting, a ceremonial instrument type long used by Kwakwaka'wakw and neighboring Northwest Coast peoples; nothing here contradicts the Kwakwaka'wakw attribution.

physical.title: rattle
physical.summary: Rattle, of alder or maple wood, carved in five parts: the body of the rattle, with the belly sliced away to be hollowed out for the rattle, and two wings, and a tail, glued on. The bird is Thunderbird-like, with a second, possibly hawk, on the belly, the beak being a separate piece of wood glued on. The rattle is painted black and red in rather archaic formline designs, with no secondary carving of details. The handle has either been deliberately darkened, or darkened in use. It is signed 'Andrew Beans March 30 1981'
